passages.text: When Ephraim spoke, there was trembling; he was exalted in Israel. But he incurred guilt through Baal, and he died.
passages.sermon:
Ephraim was a tribe in Israel.
When Ephraim spoke, people trembled.
Ephraim was important in Israel.
Ephraim worshiped Baal.
Ephraim became guilty because of Baal.
Ephraim died.
passages.original: כְּדַבֵּ֤ר אֶפְרַ֙יִם֙ רְתֵ֔ת נָשָׂ֥א ה֖וּא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֶּאְשַׁ֥ם בַּבַּ֖עַל וַיָּמֹֽת׃

passages.text: Now they sin more and more and make for themselves cast images, idols skillfully made from their silver, all of them the work of craftsmen. People say of them, “They offer human sacrifice and kiss the calves!”
passages.sermon:
The people of Ephraim sin more and more.
They make cast images for themselves.
They use their silver to make these idols.
Craftsmen skillfully make all these idols.
All the idols are the work of human hands.
People speak about these idols.
They say, “They offer human sacrifice.”
They say, “They kiss the calves.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֣ה׀ יוֹסִ֣פוּ לַחֲטֹ֗א וַיַּעְשׂ֣וּ לָהֶם֩ מַסֵּכָ֨ה מִכַּסְפָּ֤ם כִּתְבוּנָם֙ עֲצַבִּ֔ים מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה חָרָשִׁ֖ים כֻּלֹּ֑ה לָהֶם֙ הֵ֣ם אֹמְרִ֔ים זֹבְחֵ֣י אָדָ֔ם עֲגָלִ֖ים יִשָּׁקֽוּן׃

passages.text: Therefore they will be like the morning mist, like the early dew that vanishes, like chaff blown from a threshing floor, like smoke through an open window.
passages.sermon:
God judged the people of Israel for their sin.
They will disappear quickly.
They will be like the morning mist.
They will be like the early dew that vanishes.
They will be like chaff blown away from a threshing floor.
They will be like smoke that escapes through an open window.
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן יִֽהְיוּ֙ כַּעֲנַן־ בֹּ֔קֶר וְכַטַּ֖ל מַשְׁכִּ֣ים הֹלֵ֑ךְ כְּמֹץ֙ יְסֹעֵ֣ר מִגֹּ֔רֶן וּכְעָשָׁ֖ן מֵאֲרֻבָּֽה׃

passages.text: Yet I am the LORD your God ever since the land of Egypt; you know no God but Me, for there is no Savior besides Me.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
He brought you out of the land of Egypt.
You must know no other god except Him.
There is no Savior except the LORD.
passages.original: וְאָנֹכִ֛י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וֵאלֹהִ֤ים זֽוּלָתִי֙ לֹ֣א תֵדָ֔ע וּמוֹשִׁ֥יעַ אַ֖יִן בִּלְתִּֽי׃

passages.text: I knew you in the wilderness, in the land of drought.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Israel.
God says, "I knew you."
This happened in the wilderness.
The wilderness was a dry land.
The land had no water.
The land was a place of hardship.
God knew Israel during this difficult time.

passages.text: When they had pasture, they became satisfied; when they were satisfied, their hearts became proud, and as a result they forgot Me.
passages.sermon:
God cared for the people of Israel.
He gave them pasture.
They ate and became satisfied.
When they were satisfied, their hearts became proud.
Because they became proud, they forgot God.
passages.original: כְּמַרְעִיתָם֙ וַיִּשְׂבָּ֔עוּ שָׂבְע֖וּ וַיָּ֣רָם לִבָּ֑ם עַל־ כֵּ֖ן שְׁכֵחֽוּנִי׃

passages.text: So like a lion I will pounce on them; like a leopard I will lurk by the path.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Israel.
God compares Himself to a lion.
God says, "I will pounce on them like a lion."
God also compares Himself to a leopard.
God says, "I will lurk by the path like a leopard."
passages.original: וָאֱהִ֥י לָהֶ֖ם כְּמוֹ־ שָׁ֑חַל כְּנָמֵ֖ר עַל־ דֶּ֥רֶךְ אָשֽׁוּר׃

passages.text: Like a bear robbed of her cubs I will attack them, and I will tear open their chests. There I will devour them like a lion, like a wild beast would tear them apart.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Israel.
God says, "I will meet them like a bear robbed of her cubs.
I will attack them fiercely.
I will tear open their chests.
There I will devour them like a lion.
A wild beast will tear them apart."
passages.original: אֶפְגְּשֵׁם֙ כְּדֹ֣ב שַׁכּ֔וּל וְאֶקְרַ֖ע סְג֣וֹר לִבָּ֑ם וְאֹכְלֵ֥ם שָׁם֙ כְּלָבִ֔יא חַיַּ֥ת הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה תְּבַקְּעֵֽם׃

passages.text: You are destroyed, O Israel, because you are against Me— against your helper.
passages.sermon:
Israel, you are destroyed.
You are destroyed because you oppose Me.
I am your helper.
You turned against your helper.

passages.text: Where is your king now to save you in all your cities, and the rulers to whom you said, “Give me a king and princes”?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Israel.
God asks Israel a question.
God says, "Where is your king now?"
God says, "Can your king save you in all your cities?"
God says, "Where are your rulers?"
God reminds Israel, "You said, 'Give me a king and princes.'"
God shows that Israel asked for human leaders.
God shows that these leaders cannot save Israel.
passages.original: אֱהִ֤י מַלְכְּךָ֙ אֵפ֔וֹא וְיוֹשִֽׁיעֲךָ֖ בְּכָל־ עָרֶ֑יךָ וְשֹׁ֣פְטֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֔רְתָּ תְּנָה־ לִּ֖י מֶ֥לֶךְ וְשָׂרִֽים׃

passages.text: So in My anger I gave you a king, and in My wrath I took him away.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Israel.
God gave Israel a king.
God acted in anger when He gave the king.
God took the king away from Israel.
God acted in wrath when He took the king away.
passages.original: אֶֽתֶּן־ לְךָ֥ מֶ֙לֶךְ֙ בְּאַפִּ֔י וְאֶקַּ֖ח בְּעֶבְרָתִֽי׃ס

passages.text: The iniquity of Ephraim is bound up; his sin is stored up.
passages.sermon:
Ephraim is a tribe in Israel.
Ephraim has committed iniquity.
God has bound up Ephraim’s iniquity.
Ephraim has sinned.
God has stored up Ephraim’s sin.

passages.text: Labor pains come upon him, but he is an unwise son. When the time arrives, he fails to present himself at the opening of the womb.
passages.sermon:
Ephraim is a tribe in Israel.
Ephraim faces judgment for sin.
Labor pains come upon Ephraim.
Ephraim is like a son.
This son is not wise.
The time for birth arrives.
The son does not come to the opening of the womb.
He fails to be born when he should.
passages.original: חֶבְלֵ֥י יֽוֹלֵדָ֖ה יָבֹ֣אוּ ל֑וֹ הוּא־ בֵן֙ לֹ֣א חָכָ֔ם כִּֽי־ עֵ֥ת לֹֽא־ יַעֲמֹ֖ד בְּמִשְׁבַּ֥ר בָּנִֽים׃

passages.text: I will ransom them from the power of Sheol; I will redeem them from Death. Where, O Death, are your plagues? Where, O Sheol, is your sting? Compassion is hidden from My eyes.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Israel.
God promises to act.
God says, “I will ransom them from the power of Sheol.”
God says, “I will redeem them from Death.”
God asks, “Where are your plagues, Death?”
God asks, “Where is your sting, Sheol?”
God says, “Compassion is hidden from My eyes.”
passages.original: מִיַּ֤ד שְׁאוֹל֙ אֶפְדֵּ֔ם מִמָּ֖וֶת אֶגְאָלֵ֑ם אֱהִ֨י דְבָרֶיךָ֜ מָ֗וֶת אֱהִ֤י קָֽטָבְךָ֙ שְׁא֔וֹל נֹ֖חַם יִסָּתֵ֥ר מֵעֵינָֽי׃

passages.text: Although he flourishes among his brothers, an east wind will come— a wind from the LORD rising up from the desert. His fountain will fail, and his spring will run dry. The wind will plunder his treasury of every precious article.
passages.sermon:
He is a man who prospers among his brothers.
The LORD will send an east wind from the desert.
This wind will come upon him.
His fountain will dry up.
His spring will become empty.
The wind will take away every precious thing from his treasury.
passages.original: כִּ֣י ה֔וּא בֵּ֥ן אַחִ֖ים יַפְרִ֑יא יָב֣וֹא קָדִים֩ ר֨וּחַ יְהוָ֜ה מִמִּדְבָּ֣ר עֹלֶ֗ה וְיֵב֤וֹשׁ מְקוֹרוֹ֙ וְיֶחֱרַ֣ב מַעְיָנ֔וֹ ה֣וּא יִשְׁסֶ֔ה אוֹצַ֖ר כָּל־ כְּלִ֥י חֶמְדָּֽה׃

passages.text: Samaria will bear her guilt because she has rebelled against her God. They will fall by the sword; their little ones will be dashed to pieces, and their pregnant women ripped open.
passages.sermon:
Samaria is a city in Israel.
Samaria has rebelled against her God.
Samaria will bear her guilt.
The people of Samaria will fall by the sword.
Their little ones will be dashed to pieces.
Their pregnant women will be ripped open.
passages.original: תֶּאְשַׁם֙ שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן כִּ֥י מָרְתָ֖ה בֵּֽאלֹהֶ֑יהָ בַּחֶ֣רֶב יִפֹּ֔לוּ עֹלְלֵיהֶ֣ם יְרֻטָּ֔שׁוּ וְהָרִיּוֹתָ֖יו יְבֻקָּֽעוּ׃פ
